title: Israel resumes large-scale airstrikes on Gaza, ending the ceasefire that began in January
body:
In the early hours of Tuesday 18 March 2025, Israel carried out a wave of airstrikes across Gaza, ending a ceasefire that had been in effect since 19 January 2025. CNN reported that the strikes began at about 2 a.m. local time and were the most extensive since the truce began. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said: "Tonight we returned to fighting in Gaza." The Israeli military later announced a massive offensive and ordered civilians in several neighborhoods to evacuate.

The Palestinian Ministry of Health in Gaza reported at least 404 people killed and more than 562 injured. Gaza Civil Defense spokesman Mahmoud Basal told CNN that more than 130 children were among the dead. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said Israel would act against Hamas with increasing military strength. An Israeli official described the strikes as preemptive. Israel accused Hamas of repeatedly refusing to release hostages and of rejecting offers from US envoy Steve Witkoff. According to White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, Israel notified the Trump administration before the strikes.

Hamas accused Netanyahu of ending the ceasefire and endangering the captives, and rejected Israeli claims that it was preparing attacks. Of the 251 people taken hostage on 7 October 2023, nearly 60 remained in Gaza, with fewer than half believed to be alive. UN refugee agency chief Philippe Lazzarini warned that a return to war would bring more suffering. Israel had blocked food and aid from entering Gaza for about two weeks before the strikes and had cut power to the last facility still receiving electricity.
